title: What Hot-Swap Everything Is
definition: Hot-Swap Everything: replacing any code without restarting.
description:
Hot-Swap Everything: replacing any code without restarting. This is Future Software Paradigms at its most ambitious — state migration research, swap logistics engineering and version coexistence operations converging on a single goal: making swap hulls real.

Why it matters: Future Software Paradigms will decide rollback plans outcomes this century. Hot-Swap Everything is one of the load-bearing ideas: without working swap hulls, the larger state migration vision stalls, and with it, the swap logistics systems that depend on it.

This database documents Hot-Swap Everything in full: what it is, the real research behind it today, the pieces it is built from, dated forecasts, runnable demo programs, and a teaching ladder from foundations to mastery. Every record carries a working program you can run.

title: Real Research Today: Hot-Swap Everything
definition: Today's documented research behind Hot-Swap Everything.
description:
The road to Hot-Swap Everything is already being paved. Unikernel and library-OS research (MirageOS) rebuilds operating systems as composable libraries. DARPA's AI Forward and CodePro programs explore AI-assisted software engineering.

Formal methods adoption grows in aerospace (NASA), chips (Intel/ARM) and crypto protocols. Together these programs form the state migration foundation that Hot-Swap Everything will build on — the swap logistics results, the version coexistence methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as swap logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: Readiness Estimator: Hot-Swap Everything
definition: Estimates Hot-Swap Everything readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Hot-Swap Everything components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a swap hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

definition: Simulates Hot-Swap Everything operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Hot-Swap Everything installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 37356 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where state migration monitoring, swap logistics redundancy, or version coexistence maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Hot-Swap Everything Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Hot-Swap Everything: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Hot-Swap Everything — replacing any code without restarting.

Phase 1 — Prove (state migration): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (swap logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (version coexistence): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (rollback plans): swap hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and production-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
